land.text: Tiberias, taken by Daher al-Umar in 1730 with Saqr Bedouin support; Galilee, under Ottoman rule

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws Galilee inside its Ottoman Empire shape. Formal status was that of a multazim (tax farmer); in 1768 the imperial government granted him the title of Sheikh of Acre.

land.text: Acre transferred by Hasan Pasha to Ahmad al-Jazzar on 19 September 1775; Galilee after Deir Hanna fell in 1776; part of Sidon Eyalet, with Acre as Jazzar's seat

successors.note: The Jazzar page: Deir Hanna surrendered in June 1776; the Daher page: 22 July 1776.

capitals.name: Tiberias
capitals.note: 'Tiberias became his base after he took it in 1730'; the page names no formal capital before the move.

capitals.name: Acre (Akko)
capitals.note: He 'moved his headquarters from Deir Hanna to Acre around 1750'; he took Acre in 1744 and was made its multazim in July 1746.

capitals.name: Deir Hanna
capitals.note: His son Ali held Galilee from the fortified headquarters at Deir Hanna until it fell on 22 July 1776.

rulers.name: Daher al-Umar al-Zaydani
rulers.title: Sheikh of Acre
rulers.note: Died 21 or 22 August 1775 (the page says uncertain); granted the title Sheikh of Acre, Emir of Nazareth, Tiberias and Safed, and Sheikh of all Galilee in 1768.

rulers.name: Ali ibn Daher
rulers.title: Sheikh of Galilee
rulers.note: Held Galilee until Deir Hanna fell on 22 July 1776; assassinated in November 1776, 'the end of Zaydani power'.

correction.text: Tiberias and its surroundings, taken in 1730

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the state). The page gives no area; the 30 km radius is the researcher's.

correction.text: Tiberias with Jiddin, Abu Sinan and Tarshiha in western Galilee, gained in 1738

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Defeated Ahmad al-Husayn and gained Jiddin, Abu Sinan and Tarshiha' (1738).

correction.text: Tiberias, western Galilee, Safed (c. 1740) and Nazareth (by the end of 1740)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Sulayman Pasha al-Azm besieged Tiberias for 90 days in 1742-43 and died in August 1743.

correction.text: the same with Acre, taken 'probably' in 1744 and the headquarters from about 1750

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. He was formally appointed Acre's multazim in July 1746.

correction.text: with Haifa, Tira, Tantura and Mount Carmel (1757); the Metawalis of Jabal Amil as vassal from 1767 (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. An Ottoman attempt to retake Haifa failed in May 1761. 'In 1768 the imperial government granted him the title of Sheikh of Acre, Emir of Nazareth, Tiberias and Safed, and Sheikh of all Galilee.'

correction.text: the high-water mark: Galilee and Acre with Sidon (June 1771), Jaffa (August 1771, retaken 16 February 1773), Gaza and Ramla (1770-71), held with Ali Bey of Egypt

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'With Ali Bey's forces, cleared Gaza and Ramla and occupied Jaffa' (1770-1771); 'took Sidon in June 1771 and held it from October 1771'. The pages do not say how long Gaza, Ramla and Jaffa were held, so the southern coast is drawn for the whole span.

correction.text: Galilee under Ali ibn Daher at Deir Hanna, without Acre (to Jazzar, September 1775)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Abu al-Dhahab took Gaza, Ramla and Jaffa in May 1775 and Acre on 30 May; Daher re-entered Acre on 12 June; Hasan Pasha's flotilla reached Haifa on 7 August; Daher fled Acre on 22 August 1775.

ledger.note: 1730: Daher al-Umar takes Tiberias. 'Tiberias became his base after he took it in 1730' with Saqr Bedouin support; he became the paramount sheikh of the Zayadina and ruler of northern Palestine 'from the 1730s' under Ottoman rule.
1738: western Galilee. He 'defeated Ahmad al-Husayn and gained Jiddin, Abu Sinan and Tarshiha'; Sulayman Pasha al-Azm's attack that year was abortive.
c. 1740: Safed and Nazareth. He took Safed c. 1740 and 'Nazareth came under his control by the end of 1740'.
1744: Acre. He 'took Acre by force, probably in this year', and was formally appointed its multazim in July 1746.
c. 1750: the headquarters move from Deir Hanna to Acre (Deir Hanna was his sons' and brother Sa'd's fortified base).

region.text: Haifa, Tira, Tantura and Mount Carmel

ledger.note: 1757: Haifa and Mount Carmel. He 'took Haifa, Tira, Tantura and Mount Carmel'; an Ottoman attempt to retake Haifa failed in May 1761.
1767: the Metawalis of Jabal Amil. He 'allied with the Metawalis of Jabal Amil, effectively becoming their multazim'.
1770-1771: Gaza and Ramla, then Jaffa. 'With Ali Bey's forces, cleared Gaza and Ramla and occupied Jaffa'; Ali Bey's campaign began in November 1770.
June 1771: Sidon. He 'took Sidon in June 1771 and held it from October 1771'.
August 1771: Jaffa. He 'captured Jaffa and garrisoned it with 2,000 men'.
1772: Jaffa is lost. The page says Daher 'recaptured Jaffa on 16 February 1773', so it was lost earlier; neither page dates the loss (bridging, page silent).
16 February 1773: Jaffa retaken. 'Daher recaptured Jaffa on 16 February 1773 and sent his son Salibi to support Ali Bey.'

1775: Daher's death ends the Metawali alliance. The pages are silent on when the arrangement ended; the Jazzar page says Jazzar 'defeated Nasif al-Nassar in 1781, bringing Jabal Amil under his control'. Bridging judgment.
May 1775: Abu al-Dhahab invades. 'May 1775: Abu al-Dhahab's campaign took Gaza, Ramla, and Jaffa'; Acre surrendered to a small mamluk naval force on 30 May 1775.
May 1775: Gaza, Ramla and Jaffa fall to Egypt. 'Jaffa's men were executed.'
30 May 1775: Acre surrenders. 'Acre surrendered to a small mamluk naval force on 30 May 1775, and Abu al-Dhahab appointed Murad Bey as governor.'
12 June 1775: Daher re-enters Acre. 'After Abu al-Dhahab died on 10 June, Daher reentered Acre on 12 June.'
12 June 1775: the Egyptian invasion ends with Abu al-Dhahab's death on 10 June; Gaza, Ramla and Jaffa stay lost.
7 August 1775: Hasan Pasha's flotilla arrives at Haifa and then Acre, bombarding it.

19 September 1775: Acre passes to Jazzar. Daher 'fled Acre on 22 August 1775' and was shot; 'Hasan Pasha transferred Acre to Ahmad al-Jazzar on 19 September 1775' (Jazzar page: 'In September 1775 ... appointed muhafiz of Acre').
22 July 1776: Deir Hanna falls. Ali held Galilee 'until Deir Hanna fell on 22 July 1776'; the Jazzar page says Deir Hanna surrendered in June 1776.

region.text: the Galilee sheikhdom at its end

ledger.note: July 1776: the Zaydani sheikhdom ends. Ali ibn Daher was assassinated in November 1776, 'the end of Zaydani power'; Jazzar governed Sidon Eyalet from Acre.

wars.name: Ottoman campaigns against Daher al-Umar (1738-1743)
wars.outcome: Sulayman Pasha al-Azm's abortive attack (1738); Ibrahim Pasha of Sidon beaten near Acre (1741); the 90-day siege of Tiberias (September 1742-1743), Sulayman dying in August 1743.

wars.name: Daher and Ali Bey against Damascus (1770-1773)
wars.outcome: Ali Bey's campaign began in November 1770; Daher cleared Gaza and Ramla, took Jaffa (August 1771) and Sidon (June 1771); Abu al-Dhahab went over to the Ottomans in 1772; Daher retook Jaffa on 16 February 1773; Ali Bey died in 1773. Russian ships bombarded Beirut at his direction in June 1772 and July 1773.
wars.note: The Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774) kept the Ottomans busy until the peace of July 1774.

wars.name: Abu al-Dhahab's Palestine campaign
wars.outcome: May 1775: Gaza, Ramla, Jaffa taken; Acre surrendered 30 May; Abu al-Dhahab died on 10 June; Daher re-entered Acre on 12 June.
wars.note: See the mamluk-beys-of-egypt dossier for the Egyptian side.

wars.name: Hasan Pasha's campaign against Acre
wars.outcome: Hasan Pasha's flotilla reached Haifa on 7 August 1775 and bombarded Acre; Daher was killed on 22 August; Acre went to Jazzar on 19 September; Ali held Galilee until Deir Hanna fell in June or on 22 July 1776.
wars.note: The Daher page says Hasan Pasha transferred Acre on 19 September 1775; the Jazzar page says 'In September 1775'. The two pages disagree on the Deir Hanna date (22 July vs June 1776).

certainty.note: Tax-farm (iltizam) territories held by a sheikh, drawn as radii around towns; no boundary is described. The Jabal Amil arrangement is a tax-farming alliance.

sources.title: Daher al-Umar
sources.note: Identity, 1730-1775, the capitals, every gain (Tiberias 1730, Safed/Nazareth c.1740, Acre 1744, Haifa 1757, Sidon/Jaffa/Gaza/Ramla 1770-71), the 1775 collapse, Ali ibn Daher to 1776.

sources.title: Ahmad Pasha al-Jazzar
sources.note: Acre to Jazzar in September 1775, Deir Hanna June 1776, Jabal Amil 1781, Sidon Eyalet.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (Galilee sits in its Ottoman Empire shape); the slug sheikhdom-of-acre is named as counterpart in mamluk-beys-of-egypt. Wikipedia has no 'Sheikhdom of Acre' article (the title did not load); the person's article Daher al-Umar is the source, so the wikipedia field names it. Formal status was a multazim's (tax farmer); the 1768 imperial title (Sheikh of Acre, Emir of Nazareth, Tiberias and Safed, Sheikh of all Galilee) and January 1775 pardon make him an Ottoman tax farmer in law and a de facto prince; whether the Ottoman Empire dossier should record a vassal relationship is open. Counterpart 'Ahmad al-Husayn' (1738) and 'Metawalis of Jabal Amil' are strings. Two pages opened (the budget allows up to five for 7 keyframes); the gaps are the Ottoman-side wars of 1738-1743 (no frontier effect) and any page on the 1768 title. The 1776 Deir Hanna date differs between pages. Tiberias and Safed coordinates (lon/lat radii) because the gazetteer lacks them.
